_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Côte d'Ivoire covering Kong Empire, French colonisation, Houphouët-Boigny era, civil wars, and cocoa economy.

ethnic_groups.name: Akan (Baoulé, Agni, Abron, Attie)
ethnic_groups.notes: Central and eastern; Baoulé are largest sub-group; matrilineal heritage; gold traditions

ethnic_groups.name: Krou (Bété, Dida, Guéré, Wobé)
ethnic_groups.notes: Southwestern forest zone; historically strong in military and opposition politics; Gbagbo's base

ethnic_groups.name: Northern Mandé (Dioula, Malinké, Bambara)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern savanna; Muslim trading communities; Dioula lingua franca of markets; Kong Empire heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Voltaic/Gur (Sénoufo, Lobi, Koulango)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Côte d'Ivoire; Sénoufo with Poro society; farming communities

ethnic_groups.name: Southern Mandé (Dan/Yacouba, Gouro, Mano)
ethnic_groups.notes: Western forest zone; mask traditions; Man region

ethnic_groups.name: Lagoon peoples (Ebrié, Adié, Atté)
ethnic_groups.notes: Coastal lagoon zone around Abidjan; historically displaced by Akan migration

ethnic_groups.name: Foreign-origin residents
ethnic_groups.notes: Large immigrant population from Burkina Faso, Mali, Guinea; politically sensitive 'Ivoirité' debates

natural_resources.notes: World's largest cocoa producer (40% of global supply); cashew world #1; major rubber/palm oil/coffee producer; offshore oil/gas growing; gold mining expanding (Ity mine); 'chocolate nation' paradox—most cocoa workers have never tasted chocolate

military.notes: FACI (Armed Forces of Côte d'Ivoire) rebuilt after 2002-11 crisis; French forces (Variétés base) reduced; UN ONUCI peacekeeping departed 2017; former rebels integrated into army; jailé mutinies (demobilization issues)

debt_aid.notes: Fastest-growing large African economy (~7% annually); Ouattara's Plan National de Développement; Chinese infrastructure investment; CFA franc currency ties to France; Eurobond issuer

education.notes: French-language instruction; 'ivoirité' identity politics affected education access for northern/immigrant populations; school feeding programs expanding enrollment; PASEC assessment participant; gender gap persistent in rural areas

diaspora_migration.notes: Immigration hub—26% of population is foreign-born (Burkinabè, Malians, Guineans); ivoirité concept ('who is Ivorian?') xenophobic tensions central to 2002-11 conflict; Liberian/Sierra Leonean refugees from 1990s wars came to CdI

digital_economy.mobile_money_adoption: Very high (Orange Money, MTN MoMo, Wave)
tech_hubs: Abidjan (Abidjan Tech Hub, MEST Africa Hub)
digital_economy.notes: Mobile money revolution (Wave disrupted market with zero-fee transfers); Abidjan emerging as West African tech capital; strong startup ecosystem; fibre backbone improving; government digitization push; cocoa traceability blockchain pilots

current_leader.name: Alassane Ouattara
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Former IMF deputy director; won 2010 election contested by Gbagbo; re-elected 2015; controversial third term 2020

former_leaders.name: Félix Houphouët-Boigny
former_leaders.notes: Founding father; 33-year rule; architect of 'Ivorian miracle'; died in office; built Basilica of Yamoussoukro

former_leaders.name: Henri Konan Bédié
former_leaders.notes: Speaker who succeeded Houphouët; introduced 'Ivoirité'; ousted by coup

former_leaders.name: Robert Guéï
former_leaders.notes: Military coup leader; killed during 2002 civil war

former_leaders.name: Laurent Gbagbo
former_leaders.notes: First opposition-elected president; refused to leave after 2010 election loss; ICC charges (acquitted 2019)

910.name: Prehistoric Côte d'Ivoire
910.description: Early human settlement in forest and savanna zones; Neolithic and early iron-working cultures.

sub_clusters.name: Neolithic Forest and Savanna Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Hunter-gatherer communities; gradual transition to agriculture in the forest-savanna ecotone.

sub_clusters.name: Early Iron Age
sub_clusters.description: Iron-smelting evidence; early farming and forest clearance.

920.name: Early Kingdoms and Peoples
920.description: Senufo, Akan, and Mande peoples; gold and kola trade; proto-state formation.

sub_clusters.name: Senufo and Northern Peoples
sub_clusters.description: Senufo agricultural communities; Poro secret society; links to Mande trading networks.

sub_clusters.name: Akan Peoples and Gold Trade
sub_clusters.description: Baoulé, Agni, and other Akan groups; gold mining; kola nut trade.

930.name: Kong Empire
930.description: Juula Kong Empire; Islamic scholarship; trans-Saharan trade terminus; Samori destruction.

sub_clusters.name: Foundation of Kong
sub_clusters.description: Sekou Ouattara founds Kong Empire; Juula commercial network; Islamic learning centre.

sub_clusters.name: Kong Decline and Samori's Destruction
sub_clusters.description: Internal fragmentation; Samori Ture's forces sack and burn Kong 1897.

930.name: European Coastal Contact
930.description: Portuguese, Dutch, French contact; ivory trade coast; early French trading posts.

sub_clusters.name: Ivory Coast Trade Era
sub_clusters.description: European traders name the coast for ivory; limited penetration inland.

sub_clusters.name: Early French Trading Posts
sub_clusters.description: French treaties with coastal chiefs; Assinie and Grand-Bassam established.

940.name: French Colonial Côte d'Ivoire
940.description: French colony established; plantation economy; forced labour; Syndicat Agricole Africain.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Conquest and Pacification
sub_clusters.description: Colony proclaimed 1893; resistance from Baoulé, Abbey, Bété; forced pacification campaigns.

sub_clusters.name: Cocoa and Coffee Plantation Economy
sub_clusters.description: Forced labour for European planters; African cocoa farmers organise under Houphouët-Boigny.

sub_clusters.name: SAA and PDCI Origins
sub_clusters.description: Syndicat Agricole Africain 1944; PDCI-RDA founded 1946; Houphouët-Boigny leads toward autonomy.

950.name: Houphouët-Boigny Era (Ivorian Miracle)
950.description: Independence; single-party rule; cocoa-driven 'Ivorian Miracle'; Basilica of Yamoussoukro; economic crisis.

sub_clusters.name: Independence and Single-Party State
sub_clusters.description: Independence 7 August 1960; Houphouët-Boigny president; PDCI single party.

sub_clusters.name: Ivorian Economic Miracle
sub_clusters.description: Cocoa/coffee boom; 7% annual growth; Françafrique ties; migrant labour from Upper Volta.

sub_clusters.name: Economic Decline and Austerity
sub_clusters.description: Commodity price crash; structural adjustment; Basilica of Yamoussoukro built amid crisis.

sub_clusters.name: Ivoirité Origins
sub_clusters.description: Multiparty politics; ethno-nationalist 'Ivoirité' concept emerges; north-south tensions.

960.name: Post-Houphouët Crisis and Civil Wars
960.description: Bédié Ivoirité; Guéï coup; Gbagbo presidency; First and Second Ivorian Civil Wars.

sub_clusters.name: Bédié and Guéï Instability
sub_clusters.description: Bédié excludes Ouattara; Christmas Eve coup 1999; Guéï's brief rule.

sub_clusters.name: First Ivorian Civil War
sub_clusters.description: Country split north-south; Forces Nouvelles rebel north; Linas-Marcoussis accords; French Licorne.

sub_clusters.name: Second Ivorian Civil War
sub_clusters.description: Gbagbo refuses election loss to Ouattara; Battle of Abidjan; ICC arrest.

960.name: Ouattara Era and Reconstruction
960.description: Economic recovery; infrastructure boom; cocoa reforms; third-term controversy.

sub_clusters.name: Economic Recovery and Growth
sub_clusters.description: 8% growth rates; Abidjan construction boom; world's largest cocoa producer.

sub_clusters.name: Reconciliation Challenges
sub_clusters.description: Victor's justice debates; Gbagbo ICC acquittal and return; ethnic tensions persist.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
